titleStmt.title: Shiji 史记 · 秦昭襄王五十六年: notes

div.interp: The fifty-sixth and last year of King Zhaoxiang of Qin, 251 BC.
我: the Table speaks from the standpoint of the state whose column it is, so "our army" is Yan's; the subject of 伐趙, "attacked Zhao", is likewise Yan.
The fourth year of King Xi of Yan, 251 BC; the text calls him "the present king" (今王).
四战之国: the Zhengyi: Zhao borders Yan to the east, Qin to the west, Han and Wei to the south and the Hu and Mo to the north, hence "at war on four sides".
The Suoyin: five men against one.

The Suoyin and the Zhengyi cite the Zhanguoce, which differs: Lian Po met Li Fu at Hao with two hundred thousand men, Yue Cheng met Qing Qin at Dai with fifty thousand, and the men of Yan were heavily defeated. The Zhanguoce writes the general's name 爰秦 (Suoyin) or 庆秦 (Zhengyi).
The Suoyin: Zhao wished to have Jiang Qu put in charge of making the peace; the Jijie: Yan made Jiang Qu its Chancellor.
The twelfth year of King Kaolie of Chu, 251 BC.
The fifteenth year of King Xiaocheng of Zhao, 251 BC.
尉文: the Suoyin: probably a place name, or else 尉 an office and 文 a name, the grant being the land that Wen had held; the Zhengyi: probably land in Weizhou.
The Hereditary House of Yan, above, has Yue Jian flee to Zhao.
The twenty-sixth year of King Anxi of Wei, 251 BC.
The twenty-second year of King Huanhui of Han, 251 BC.
